onset_repairs.rationale: Said must equal shown at the first phrase: the first spoken word (onset 1.42 s) had no visual until the window opened at 1.95 s. The field's recorded fix — windows open at first-word onset at the next plan rebuild — is executed by this repair; the re-probe measures word 1 visible at its onset within probe precision.
onset_repairs.record: REPAIRED 2026-10-26 (JOB ONSET-REPAIR-1). The defect: PLAN phrase-1 window opened at 1.95 s while the first word's spoken onset (its PLAN word start) is 1.42 s — +530 ms (measured by JOB PACKAGE-VERIFY-2's playback probe; this job's baseline probe of the unmodified scene, same method, first saw word 1 "A" at audioT 2.108 s). The change, confined to the opening timing (byte-exact reconstruction check: the repaired scene differs from the branch master by exactly these two values and nothing else): (1) PLAN phrases[0].start 1.9500000000000002 -> 1.42 — the phrase-1 window now opens at the first word's spoken onset; the word's own start (1.42 s) already equalled its onset and did not move; (2) the render loop's opening-card gate `if (t < 1.6)` -> `if (t < 1.42)` — the gate is the early return that suppresses ALL phrase rendering while the opening card holds, so at 1.6 s it would have kept word 1 invisible until 1.6 s (+180 ms residual); it is the phrase-1 window's outer gate and moved with it. PLAN timeline[0][0] deliberately NOT moved (1.95 s): it drives line-1 progress, plate zoom and label predicates for the whole line, and lineAt() already returns line 0 before it; the offset was a phrase-window defect, not a line-window one. Words 2+ carry independent starts and were not touched. Re-probe of the repaired scene (same probe, private port): word 1 first visible at audioT 1.505 s — residual +85 ms against the 1.42 s onset, within the probe's own precision (150 ms poll step; the verify jobs' first-visible readings scatter +21..+188 ms around known onsets, and words 2-4 re-probed unchanged within the same scatter); zero page exceptions. The candidate render was re-rendered from the repaired scene with the house capture (renderAt at 30 fps, libx264 CRF 19 — the delivered encode) and the package's verified clone programme audio stream copied byte-identical (sha256 of the stream equals audio/narration.m4a): new render sha256 ac79636898b9dcb73274ef5d0c88820086e83f4ef2d2285bcf33712ee14e1a28, 26007231 B, duration 62.34 s, 1870 frames, measured -14.82 LUFS / -1.3 dBTP (delivered candidate: 62.34 s, -14.82 LUFS / -1.3 dBTP). story_structure.value: Problem–Agitation–Solution (a deliberate variation from Ep.1/Ep.2's And–But–Therefore). PROBLEM: every message so far needs a living carrier (L3). AGITATION: carriers die; when the last rememberer dies, the message dies (L4). SOLUTION: put the message on the wall, where it waits for strangers (L5–L7) — at a price named in L8–L9 (it cannot travel). Villain (N-06), named: the dying witness. Intended feeling: unease in the dark of the cave, then awe.
